The Shanghai Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) declined sharply in early 2025 due to excess vessel
capacity and weaker global trade demand, before stabilizing amid market volatility.
Since late 2025, freight rates have begun to recover toward ~1500 by March 2026, driven largely by
geopolitical tensions and disruptions to key maritime routes, highlighting how global conflicts can
tighten shipping supply and create upward pressure on freight rates—an important signal for logistics,
trade, and shipping sector investment outlooks.
As of March 13, 2026, freight rates have increased by 14.58% over the past seven days, rising 221.16
points from 1,489.19 to 1,710.35. When compared with the end of February 2026, the Shanghai
Containerized Freight Index (SCFI) has climbed 28.31% within less than two weeks, indicating a rapid
rebound in container freight rates. This sharp upward trend highlights increasing pressure on logistics
costs, which may impact transportation budgets, supply chain planning, and pricing strategies.
In addition, this situation has led to port congestion, a shortage of containers, and rising fuel costs
Since fuel accounts for approximately 45% of maritime transportation costs, the ongoing war is likely a
major factor contributing to the increase in shipping costs in the first quarter of 2026.Current Situation
